title: Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) Planner (I) (LtCol to Capt) EMOS (0202, 0602, 1702, 1706, 7315, 7318), DC I
raw_text:
2. MOS 1704, Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) Planner (I) (LtCol
to Capt) EMOS (0202, 0602, 1702, 1706, 7315, 7318), DC I

    a. Summary. Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) Planners plan,
integrate, coordinate, supervise, de-conflict, and assess fleet marine force
(FMF) actions that exploit, attack, protect, and manage the electromagnetic
environment (EME) and electromagnetic battlespace in support of naval and FMF
objectives. EMSO Planners advocate for and integrate ground and air
offensive, defensive, and EMSO support capabilities in tactical and
operational level plans, operations, and activities in support of
information. Working primarily at the MEF information group (MIG)
information command center (ICC) electromagnetic spectrum operations cell
(EMSOC), ICC detachment EMSOCs, FMF command elements and major subordinate
command levels, EMSO Planners advise commanders and staffs on the employment
of EMSO assets that synchronize aspects of intelligence, spectrum management,
electronic attack (EA), electronic warfare support (ES), electronic
protection (EP), cyberspace warfare and space operations into the commanders
scheme of maneuver. EMSO Planners maintain relationships with EMSO system
subject matter experts (SMEs), as well as joint and coalition capability SMEs
and planners. EMSO Planners are also represented within the service
headquarters and supporting establishment to support the development and
integration of EMSO capabilities into the operating forces.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Security requirement: must meet sensitive compartmented
information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a current single scope
background investigation (SSBI)/T5 investigation.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Must complete the Cyber Electromagnetic Operations Officer Course
(A09D212) at Ft Eisenhower, GA.

        (2) Waivers to any prerequisites or requirements must be submitted to
and approved by the 1700 occupational field manager, HQMC DC I, IMD.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Intelligence Officer, 0202.

            (2) Aviation Electromagnetic Spectrum Officer, 0588.

            (3) Communications Officer, 0602.

            (4) Strategic Electromagnetic Spectrum Officer, 0640.

            (5) Cyberspace Warfare Officer, 1702.

            (6) Maritime Space Officer, 1706.



                                          1-83                       Enclosure (1)
 1114                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (7) Signals Intelligence/Electronic Warfare/Cyberspace Operations
Officer, 2602.

            (8) Group 3 UAS MAGTF Officer, 7315.

            (9) VMU MQ-9 Officer, 7318.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
